title: "About"

## Background

I grew up in the UK and went to McGill in Montreal for my undergraduate
degree, where I did an Honours Chemistry major. My honours project looked at
synthesising dendritic macromolecules for use in drug delivery. After
graduating I stayed on as a research assistant, continuing that project and
working alongside another group on mechanochemical synthesis.

I then left Canada for the UK and joined Merkle as a Decisioning Consultant,
eventually becoming a Lead Decisioning Architect working with clients across
Europe. From there I moved into a Modelling and Data Science Manager role.

## Why data science

Architecting decisioning systems meant I spent years close to the models that
drove them without ever owning the modelling itself, and moving into a
management role only sharpened that. As the field has evolved those models
have become steadily more central to how decisioning works, and analysing
them was consistently the part of the job I enjoyed most. I came to UBC's
Master of Data Science to build a broader and deeper foundation than I could
pick up on the job, and to work with methods I was unlikely to meet in the
marketing projects I was on.

## Outside of data science

I mainly climb, ski and golf, but I'll take on most sports that come my way.
I also game and ride motorcycles, though I don't currently own one.
